links.comparator_used: CGM with all alerts off (real-time glucose values and trend graphs still displayed passively on monitors and tablets, with a non-disableable 40 mg/dL alert)
links.outcome: Percentage of time in range (70-180 mg/dL) during hospitalization
links.effect: TIR 75.1% (SD 16.6) with audible threshold alerts vs 71.2% (SD 18.1) with alerts off; adjusted mean difference 3.9% (95% CI 0.1% to 7.8%; Holm-adjusted P = .04). Time above range >180 mg/dL was lower (-3.9%, 95% CI -7.1% to -0.7%). Time below range <70 mg/dL did not differ (-0.04%, 95% CI -0.3% to 0.2%). The benefit appeared in the daytime (4.7%) but not overnight.
links.tradeoff: The threshold-alert group generated 5163 alerts among 117 of 177 participants. Alarm burden and alarm fatigue were not assessed. The authors note that responding needs adequate staffing, and the benefit was not seen in patients on intensive insulin therapy.
links.quote: The mean (SD) TIR was significantly higher in the threshold on and prediction off group than in the threshold off and prediction off group (75.1% [16.6%] vs 71.2% [18.1%]; adjusted mean difference, 3.9% [95% CI, 0.1%-7.8%]; Holm-adjusted P = .04) ( Table 2 ).
